transcript: You know what one of my favourite new theatre trends is on Broadway is plays that are starring big celebrity names in the lead roles, but then they have a huge cast with a bunch of Broadway debuts. I am obsessed with this. We saw this last year with Goodnight and Good Luck, starring George Clooney, who was making his Broadway debut, followed by a huge ensemble cast of people also making their Broadway debuts. And we're seeing it again this year with Dog Day Afternoon. Dog Day Afternoon has a huge cast LED by Jon Bernthal and Eban Moss-Bachrach, who are making their Broadway debuts, but are also the celebrities pulling in the ticket sales. But then joining them are 18 other actors. And there are also a ton of Broadway debuts in the rest of the cast. I love this. I'm obsessed with this. And not only that, but this is a new play adapted from the film of the same name. We're seeing more plays being adapted from films also, like Good Night and Good Luck, and I don't mind it at all. I'm really excited to see how they stage this. Just recently watched Dog Day Afternoon and the entire time I was like, how do you put this on stage? I cannot wait to see it. I'm loving this trend, especially when it's so hard to sell. Especially when it's so hard to sell. New theater, especially new plays. And that one of the Only known ways to sell plays is to have a celebrity in the cast. I think a great compromise is having the celebrity in the cast and then a bunch of actors new to Broadway. I love this trend. I hope to see more of it. I think ultimately, it's a great evolution of the business as theatre producers try to figure out how to get more people to see theatre, and I think this is a really great way to do it. Also, anytime there's trans representation on Broadway, I'm happy, and we have a lot of it this year.
